form: One signed plenary merits opinion preserving ten distinct claim and procedural components; a Stone partial concurrence
authority: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela assigns from each unanimous component disposition coalition, notwithstanding his distinct rationale and procedural disposition-only agreement.
fit: Ginsburg writes for the combined work shown in her Clanton and Elder opinions: identifying personally responsible material warrant deception, retaining the complete conduct-date defense, and preventing a legal-source shorthand from becoming a Supreme-Court-only notice rule. Her McCardle opinion also distinguishes proper presentation from legal merits, directly fitting the untimely and waived components. Scalia is the strongest equal-count alternative through Smith's obvious-force analysis, but this record requires coordinating that distinct force limit with the affidavit and appellate-component boundaries, which Ginsburg's actual opinions address together. Stone is not eligible to carry the complete retained-immunity rationale; his lower or equal count could not overcome that limitation. No broadened liability, new notice premise or altered Associate commitment secures the assignment.
count_effect: One signed plenary lead counts for Ginsburg; the separate Stone concurrence adds no count.
